Subject: Weekly Fleet Planning: align pipeline forecasts to capacity sourcing

Team —

Quick kickoff for this week’s fleet planning thread. Goal: reconcile sales pipeline expectations for Nimbus Health with what infra/finance can commit to for Q2 (reserved + burst mix). High-level ask: everyone please surface the concrete numbers you need, the lead times, and any blockers by EOD Monday so we can present a recommended sourcing plan to Finance on Tuesday.

What I need from each of you:
- Laura: updated deal-staged forecast for Nimbus (pilot -> POC -> commit), ideally by model latency class (low / med / high) and tokens-per-minute estimates.
- Ben: what burst slots / temporary pools can we realistically offer within 2–6 weeks vs longer-term reserved capacity? Also provide estimated tail latency impact if we push to lower-cost hardware.
- Karthik: given the forecast, what are the minimum committed GPU-weeks to hit SLAs, and what are options for partial commitments?
- Kimberly: pricing terms and reserve discounts we can offer (and minimums) — include procurement calendar constraints.
- Jordan: any finance constraints / approval lead times for a mid-size commit; also how will this affect runway metrics if we front-load credits?

Attachments: I started a stub CSV in Drive with the Nimbus forecast columns (link below). Add your rows. I’ll aggregate on Monday morning.

Thanks — let’s keep this tight; Nimbus timeline moved up and procurement expects a clear ask next week.

—Priyom

Hi Priyom —

Uploading the Nimbus staged forecast into the Drive now. Summary highlights below (attached CSV: NIMBUS_Q2_pipeline_and_capacity.csv):
- Pilot (May 15–Jun 15): expected steady-state peak ~35 concurrent DSPs, 1.2M tokens/day; mostly med-latency models.
- POC (Jun 20–Jul 31): expected peak ~120 DSPs, 4.8M tokens/day; 70% med, 30% high-latency (long context).
- Contract/Commit (Aug onward): initial commit ask coming in at 450 DSPs equivalent for Q4 when fully ramped; financing option still TBD.

Notes: Nimbus has signaled they prefer a dedicated pool for PII-handling routes (HIPAA adjacent). They requested a canary for our dedicated offering with SLA target of p95 <= 250ms for med-latency calls.

I added columns for tokens-per-minute and per-route distribution. Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk through.

—Laura

Subject: Re: Weekly Fleet Planning: align pipeline forecasts to capacity sourcing

Folks —

I reviewed the forecast Laura uploaded. Quick operational reality check:
- Short-term (2–6 weeks): we can spin a burst pool sized to handle the Pilot (35 concurrent) using existing spare capacity and burst credits; that’s low risk.
- Medium-term (4–10 weeks): POC peak of ~120 concurrent will require either: (A) temporary burst slots + preferential scheduling across pools (higher latency tail risk), or (B) filling one small dedicated 16–32 GPU cage (lead time ~4 weeks depending on region).
- Long-term commit (450 DSPs equiv): that’s a dedicated-reserved conversation — lead time for procurement + capacity ordering is 8–12 weeks for dedicated racks in our preferred region.

Important: If we attempt to serve the POC on lower-cost instance types to save money, expect a 10–20% p95 latency degradation and potential token-per-second drop that affects throughput for long-context models. I attached infra_burst_slots_2027Q2.xlsx with the current burst inventory and estimated burn rates.

Action items from infra:
1) Approve a 4-week lead to provision a temporary 16–32 GPU cage as an option B for POC.
2) Confirm region preference (us-west vs us-east) — us-west has slightly lower lead times today.
3) If Finance approves a partial commit (3–6 month), we can negotiate earlier provisioning.

—Ben

Thanks — adding Karthik’s run-of-numbers.

Baseline SLA targets: p95 <= 250ms (med), 1s (high long-context)
Capacity math (rough):
- Pilot: reserve 10 GPU-weeks (short-term reserved + burst mix).
- POC peak: reserve 48–64 GPU-weeks distributed over the month to hit throughput targets; if we do 16–32 GPU cage, treat remaining as burst.
- Ramp to commit: recommend staged commit (Q4 ramp) with 3-month partial commit first; that reduces procurement shock and gives Nimbus lower upfront cash.

Risk notes:
- If we accept a relaxed commit (no hard minimum), finance will want higher price to offset capacity variance.
- We can trade latency for lower cost using quantized model variants for non-PHI routes; affects quality.

I can prepare two quote scenarios (A: conservative reserved-heavy; B: mixed reserved+burst with credits) if Kimberly can provide pricing ranges by EOD.

—Karthik Iyer
VP, Product Operations | Redwood Inference

Laura / Priyom —

Thanks for the summary and the CSV. A couple of clarifying items from procurement side:
1) Nimbus prefers a 6-month phased commitment if pricing is tiered — they want to avoid a large upfront Q4-only commit.
2) For HIPAA-adjacent traffic they need dedicated pools and SOC2 evidence; can Redwood provide SOC2 audit window details and a canary SLA for the med-latency routes?
3) Preferred region: us-west for latency to their East Coast users (they said us-west is acceptable).

We can aim to sign a Letter of Intent by May 21 if Redwood can present a clear committed plan and pricing.

—Monica Reyes
